note: Diagnostic for the direct freshness proof every cache-reading command runs first.
binary: cargo build --release -p vulcan-cli at each commit

machine.host: designated evaluation host (Intel Core i7-10700, 31 GiB RAM, Debian 13)

method.timing: wall clock of the whole process; 16 runs, the first discarded; p50 of 15, two interleaved rounds per binary
method.proof_cost: refresh=blocking minus refresh=off on an unchanged vault, where the proof finds the cache fresh
method.stage_profile: a temporary instrumented build (not committed) timed the proof's stages at 100K: index rows 44 ms, parallel walk 74 ms, compare 10 ms, run one after the other

findings: At 100K the proof fell from about 155 ms (228 - 73) to about 106 ms (178 - 72); at 10K from 19 to 13 ms
Output is identical; the remaining cost is mostly the parallel walk, which every file's stat requires
A daemon-hosted vault avoids the proof altogether through routed reads (`--route auto`), whose index barrier vouches for freshness
limitations: Host power, frequency, background load, and OS page cache are uncontrolled
